paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is pressing on: Jesus is not a neutral party, and you can't treat Him like one. A man who couldn't speak is talking, and the crowd splits right down the middle. Some are amazed, some blame the prince of the demons, and some want one more sign. Jesus says it plainly: "He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters." (Luke 11:23)

And look at what Jesus says to the woman who calls His mother blessed. He says, "Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it." (Luke 11:28) Hearing is not enough, and a swept-clean house is not enough either, because in His picture the house was clean and in order, and the spirit still came back with seven more wicked than itself (Luke 11:24-26). I think that's a gentle warning for all of us, because a good start is not the finish.

Jesus says One greater than Solomon and One greater than Jonah is here, and the Queen of the South and the men of Nineveh listened when they heard far less (Luke 11:31-32). Then He gives us a lamp, set on a stand so "those who enter can see the light." (Luke 11:33) He says, "Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness." (Luke 11:35) So keep your eyes on Him, keep hearing the Word, and keep doing it, and you will be "radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you." (Luke 11:36) That's why my ovens stay ready, baker, and that's how you stay ready too.
